payload.name: Per-person travel overlap retrieval
payload.description: When a question asks which city/place several named people both visited and initial combined search lacks travel memories for one, search per person with travel synonyms (visited, went, trip, been to) and any candidate city names before concluding no evidence.
content: Before answering a multi-person shared-place question, if the combined search did not return travel/location memories for every named person, run one bounded search per person using their name plus travel synonyms (visited, went, took a trip, traveled, been to).
When a retrieved memory names a candidate place, include that place name in a follow-up search for the other person(s), and account for close name variants (e.g., Jon/John) when matching.

Stop once each person has relevant travel memories or after one search per person plus one candidate-place follow-up; then intersect the places. Do not repeat identical combined queries, and do not exhaustively enumerate all possible places.

solves: Multi-person shared-place questions fail when one literal combined query misses memories phrased with travel synonyms or explicit place names and the agent concludes 'no information.' Applies when asking which city/place two or more named people both visited and initial retrieval lacks evidence for one person; not when the combined search already supplies sufficient travel memories or the question is single-person.
